title: Identity Hardening: SSO/SAML/SCIM & Least-Privilege Design — Pinecrest Finance

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Claire (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Jonas (Redwood Product Security), Leah (Pinecrest Head of Security), Marco (Platform Eng), Aisha (IAM), Samir (CISO)

Summary/Agenda (auto):
- Quick intros and objectives
- Walk through SAML mapping and SCIM provisioning expectations
- RBAC/least-privilege model walk-through using Pinecrest org examples
- Audit logs, KMS, data residency, SOC2 artifacts
- Agree next steps & owners

[00:00] Claire: okay great, thanks everyone for joining on such short notice. um the goal for today is to make sure we have alignment on SSO and provisioning patterns and then, like, the least privilege model you want to land on for Redwood-inference access.
[00:22] Leah: thanks Claire. yeah, we just want to make sure this integrates with our existing IdP and that provisioning is predictable. Our auditors will ask about log retention and who can deprovision access.
[00:35] Ravi: got it. quick intro from my side — I focus on onboarding and SCIM flows. i'll talk through mappings and the failure modes we typically see.
[00:45] Marco: quick one — we are running Okta today in a multi-tenant setup, and we have a requirement that all PII stays in eu-central. is that something Redwood supports?
[01:02] Claire: yes, we have hosted regions and private deployment options. you can pin to eu-central region and keep logs and backups in region for an additional data residency add-on, or alternatively we can do a VPC/private deployment. we'll share the region SLA doc.
[01:18] Jonas: on top of that, from a product-security perspective, we'd like to confirm key management options — bring-your-own KMS vs Redwood-managed keys and HSM-backed keys.
[01:31] Samir: the auditors, specifically for SOC2, will want control over key rotation and proof of only authorized roles having key access.
[01:40] Ravi: okay i'll show the SCIM mapping patterns. i'm going to screen-share — assume i say 'screen-share' but transcript may not capture it — we generally provision groups as roles, and map the Okta group to Redwood role-id. SCIM group sync runs every 5 minutes by default, with configurable backoff.
[01:58] Aisha: what's the retry/backoff behaviour on large orgs? we have ~14k users and hundreds of groups.
[02:08] Ravi: right, large orgs we recommend chunking group syncs and enabling batch sync. we also support incremental sync based on last-modified. in practice we've seen SCIM timeouts when >1k updates happen at once — so we surface an async webhook with status for each group.
[02:28] Marco: any rate limits we need to pre-configure on the IdP?
[02:33] Ravi: yes, Okta has a rate limit — we document recommended rate windows. we can also do a delegated sync where Redwood pulls user/group deltas from Okta, or you push via SCIM.
[02:45] Leah: on attribute mapping — we want email, role, manager, and a custom 'entitlement' claim for access to production models. how do you handle conflicting attributes?
[02:58] Ravi: attribute resolution: last-writer wins, but we support attribute precedence rules (IdP overrides or local overrides). for production sensitive roles we recommend locking attribute source to SCIM only and disallowing local edits.
[03:15] Claire: let me interject — for least-privilege we encourage role slices: environment:dev/prod; capabilities:view/infer/admin; and resource tags. so a user might be pinecrest:engineer:infer:prod.
[03:34] Leah: ok, that pattern sounds promising. how do service accounts fit? we run pipeline bots that need access for batch inference.
[03:42] Jonas: service accounts are mapped to machine principals. we recommend separate RBAC roles with time-limited tokens and no human MFA requirement. token rotation enforced via KMS policies.
[03:53] Marco: are those tokens long lived? we prefer short-lived tokens.
[03:57] Ravi: short-lived — default 1 hour for access tokens, refreshable by the service account using a private key. sessions for humans can be longer with step-up for elevated actions.
[04:08] Aisha: on SAML specifics — we want to send eduPersonEntitlement-like claims for role mapping, do you accept custom attributes?
[04:16] Claire: yes, SAML attribute mapping is configurable. we consume NameID/email as principal and map custom attributes to roles. sometimes SAML gets transcribed as 'SAMEL' in logs — minor point but watch mapping.
[04:30] Marco: what about SCIM group deletions? we need hard deletes to remove access immediately for leavers.
[04:37] Ravi: SCIM supports delete operations; we also have a deprovisioning webhook for immediate actions and an audit trail entry. by default we mark accounts disabled for 24 hours then hard-delete after 30 days, but enterprise customers can request immediate hard delete on group membership removal.
[04:56] Leah: auditors ask for immutability of audit logs. can you guarantee write-once logs or an append-only store?
[05:03] Jonas: logs are exported to our immutable event store and we can provide tamper-evidence via hash-chaining. for private deployments you can push logs to your own S3 with lifecycle policies. retention configurable to 7 years per your policy.
[05:20] Samir: we need to see sample audit reports and evidence for SOC2 controls — can you redact and share?
[05:27] Claire: yes, i'll send a redacted SOC2 Type II summary and the list of controls; it will be in the next steps.
[05:34] Marco: about KMS — we use AWS KMS with HSM-backed CMKs. do you support external key managers?
[05:42] Jonas: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault integration, and HSMs via external key manager (EKM) in private deployments. some telemetry like envelope keys still pass through Redwood for index/ops unless you choose an air-gapped on-prem install.
[05:59] Aisha: can we disable telemetry? we have strict data control requirements.
[06:05] Claire: telemetry can be minimized; we have a telemetry control matrix. for sensitive customers we can turn off non-essential metrics and route only health pings.
[06:15] Marco: any change management around role creation? we need approvals for granting admin roles.
[06:21] Ravi: RBAC change workflows support approval policies — you can require manager approval or an approval queue. we also integrate with ticketing systems for auditability.
[06:32] Leah: the last time we onboarded a vendor, there was confusion around who could create service accounts vs who could bind roles. do you support granular RBAC for role binding?
[06:41] Jonas: yes, RBAC is hierarchical. you can create a 'role-admin' role that can create roles but not assign them, and a separate 'binder' role for assignment. we expose role templates to make consistent slices.
[06:56] [07:00] Claire: i'll put an example up — we use a nomenclature of role:domain:capability:environment, and policies are additive.
[07:10] Marco: what about emergency access — break-glass?
[07:14] Ravi: break-glass is supported via time-limited emergency tokens that require two-person approval and are logged to an immutable audit event; those events are retained and can trigger pager workflows.
[07:27] Leah: regarding data residency, if we pin to eu-central, does Redwood still route auth to us or does it terminate SSO in us-east?
[07:36] Claire: for hosted eu region, SSO termination happens in eu, and logs & artifacts remain in eu. metadata for the IdP still points to regional endpoints. if you need full isolation, we recommend Redwood Private running in your VPC.
[07:52] Samir: do you have pen test or vulnerability disclosure docs we can share with security?
[07:57] Jonas: yes we publish a summary and we can share our responsible disclosure process. we also have a schedule of periodic pen tests and results summary redacted.
[08:10] Aisha: SCIM group sync — what is the conflict resolution if the same user is in two groups that map to conflicting roles?
[08:20] Ravi: we support role precedence rules and can block conflicting role assignments automatically, or surface a conflict report to your IAM admin for manual resolution. we can set precedence by group priority or by timestamp.
[08:35] Marco: are we able to map Okta attributes to resource tags for model-level access? we'd like to restrict certain models to finance only.
[08:44] Claire: yes, tag-based authorization is supported. you can create policy rules like allow(infer) if user.tag == resource.tag and environment==prod.
[08:57] Leah: auditors will want a matrix showing who had access to prod models in the last 12 months. are your logs queryable?
[09:05] Jonas: logs are queryable via our console and via exported logs to your SIEM (we have a Splunk/Datadog integration). retention and export frequency are configurable.
[09:18] Marco: about SCIM payloads — will you accept custom schemas? we have some legacy attributes.
[09:24] Ravi: yes — SCIM is extensible; we can accept custom attributes and map them to internal claims. we'll send a sample schema.
[09:33] [09:40] Claire: quick check — any blockers from Pinecrest on proceeding with a staging pilot?
[09:44] Aisha: we just need the SCIM template and an Okta metadata endpoint. also we want usage logging to be enabled in staging to validate audit trails.
[09:52] Samir: and the SOC2 summary before the pilot kicks off to satisfy our procurement legal team.
[09:59] Claire: understood. we'll provide that.
[10:05] Marco: question on SAML certificate rotation. how do you handle IdP certificate rotations without breaking sessions?
[10:12] Ravi: we support multiple active certificates — you can upload a new cert and switch over while the old one remains valid for an overlap window. sessions will remain valid until token expiry.
[10:23] Leah: are there any known edge cases with Okta scoping and nested groups? we've seen nested groups flattening issues.
[10:32] Ravi: nested groups are flattened by our sync; we preserve lineage but present effective memberships. for very deep nesting we recommend flattening at IdP side at least for critical groups to reduce churn.
[10:46] Marco: how granular are logs for SCIM operations — can we get per-user change details and who triggered them?
[10:53] Jonas: yes, SCIM logs include actor, timestamp, operation, payload diffs and originating IP. we can export diffs to your SIEM with a tamper-evident hash.
[11:10] Aisha: one of our constraints — we require that only certain people can grant the 'admin' role and that grant events are multi-signed. can Redwood enforce multi-signer approvals?
[11:22] Ravi: yes, we integrate with approval workflows; multi-signer is supported for high-risk role grants. it will create an audit event that lists signers and time.
[11:33] Leah: what's the on-call pattern if production access is accidentally escalated? can we revoke sessions immediately?
[11:39] Claire: sessions can be revoked and tokens rotated. for immediate revocation we can push a global session kill and force re-auth, and those events surface in audit logs.
[11:48] Samir: procurement wants indemnity language around data breaches and SLAs — that'll go through legal but wanted to flag it now.
[11:55] Claire: noted. we'll have legal loop in and share our standard terms and data processing addendum.
[12:05] Marco: any guidance on minimum entropy for keys or password policies you enforce?
[12:11] Jonas: we recommend NIST SP 800-63 for passphrases and enforce minimum key lengths for KMS. for service principals we recommend RSA-3072 or ECDSA P-256.
[12:24] Aisha: do you offer account takeover detection (MFA bypass) or anomalous login detection?
[12:31] Ravi: we have risk signals and can optionally enable anomaly detection that triggers step-up or blocks. it's an add-on telemetry rule set.
[12:45] Leah: going back to logs — can you provide a retention policy example and the cost if we extend to 7 years?
[12:54] Claire: yes, cost varies by region. for eu-central 7 years of logs is an add-on; we'll include sample pricing in the follow-up.
[13:05] Marco: from an operations POV we want to test a failure scenario: IdP outage. what happens to running inference requests?
[13:12] Ravi: SSO is for auth; once a session token is issued the runtime validates token locally. running inference is unaffected by IdP outage for active sessions. new logins will fail until IdP is back or a fallback SSO/backup IdP is configured. we recommend a secondary IdP or an emergency break-glass account.
[13:30] Aisha: for compliance, do you sign BAA or similar? we might have regulated data — not PII but financial transaction patterns.
[13:38] Claire: we have a BAA available for certain products; we'll surface the legal docs.
[13:45] Samir: i think that's everything from my side, mostly just wanted the SOC2 and SCIM pilot timeline.
[13:52] Claire: great — to recap next steps, we'll send the SOC2 redacted report, SCIM mapping template, proposed staging workshop times, and an RBAC pattern doc.
[14:04] Leah: thanks — can you also include a sample immutable audit export and instructions for hooking into Splunk?
[14:10] Jonas: yes i'll include the export schema and sample queries.
[14:18] Marco: i'll take ownership of standing up the Okta test tenant and will share metadata.
[14:23] Aisha: i'll compile the list of groups and desired mappings.
[14:27] Claire: perfect — final note: we'll treat telemetry and key handling per your policy during the pilot.
[14:35] [14:40] Claire: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts. end meeting.
